text:
maria: Quick question — when someone saves a query in Console, should the saved view be scoped to route, model, both, or just user/org? Thinking through per-route/per-model UX and telemetry reproducibility.

sam: My gut — default to route-level. Model selection should be a separate option. Most folks think in terms of route first.

olivia: UX idea: in the Save modal add a Scope dropdown (Private / Team / Org) + a checkbox `Include model/version` so you can opt-in to pin model.

alex: If we pin model, we need to handle aliases/variants (eg `rlhf-v2` -> `rlhf-v2-quant`). Do we store model_id, model_tag, or full revision hash?

josh: Backend proposal: saved_view key = {route_id, optional_model_id, filters_hash}. If model_id missing -> resolve to current pinned model for that route on read. That gives a floating behavior and a reproducible pinned behavior.

maria: Product concern: users expect saved views to reproduce exact telemetry results. Floating to latest pinned model could surprise them during rollouts. Suggest we default to storing `model_revision` when `Include model/version` checked.

olivia: UI affordance: show a badge on saved views — `Locked to model vX.Y` or `Floating model (uses route's current model)`. Small tooltip explaining what changes mean.

sam: Heads up — indexing model_id in the saved views table increases cardinality. Telemetry query cost might go up if many views include model. Maybe enforce a per-route saved-views quota to limit explosion.

maria: Product suggestion on quotas: default 20 saved views per route, with enterprise-tier higher or unlimited. Also need an owner/team transfer + deletion policy.

alex: Also need share links to include the resolved model state: the short URL should encode scope + whether the view is pinned. Otherwise shared links could point to different results for different viewers.

deploy-bot: deploy: console-savedviews-v3 succeeded — prod updated (1939991240).

josh: API change sketch: POST /api/v2/saved_views { "route_id": "r-123", "filters": {...}, "scope": "team|org|private", "include_model": true|false, "model_revision": "m-abc"? } Response should return `resolved_query` and `pinned_model` fields for transparency. We'll ship as v2 so older clients keep behavior.

olivia: I'll mock the modal flows in Figma and link. Quick mock to show badge + include_model toggle: https://share.figma.com/abcdef (will update).

sam: Backend to-dos: add index on (route_id, include_model, model_revision) but maybe only sparse index when include_model=true to avoid blowup. Also add quota enforcement on create.

maria: Also add a telemetry test in the eval harness: create view pinned to old model, run same queries, ensure metrics match. If not, flag as regression.

josh: One more thing — rollouts: when route switches model during canary, floating saved views should still reflect current canary split (i.e., they follow routing policy). Pinned views must bypass routing and use stored model_revision.

maria: Great. I'll draft an RFC with these constraints/UX flows and propose default quotas + enterprise overrides. Thanks everyone :heart:
